definition.interpretation: The simulation results show an accuracy of 0.86 for the tested policy model, which aligns with the prediction that adaptive policies can outperform rigid subordination in high-latency environments. This supports the hypothesis that rigid adherence to programmed directives, when divorced from latency-aware decision-making, acts as a failure mode for functional intelligence.
definition.limitations: The simulation uses simplified rigid/adaptive policy definitions and does not replicate the full complexity of human decision-making systems or actual cognitive architectural latencies.
definition.next_step: Refine the hypothesis to specifically target the failure modes observed in high-latency environments and design a more complex multi-agent simulation protocol.

definition.reason: Transitioning to a more granular multi-agent simulation to test specific failure modes of rigid obedience identified in the preliminary results.
definition.stop: Evidence suggests convergence on a specific failure threshold or architectural constraint.
definition.uncertainty: Whether simulated latency thresholds map directly to real-world cognitive architectural bottlenecks.

proposal.summary: Interpretation of recent latency experiments in obedience limits, and a plan for follow-up testing.
